name: WebSDR-Sync
description: Keeps a WebSDR tuned to your transceiver over Hamlib rigctld, and mutes it while you transmit.
//: VERSIONING
The package version is two digits -- 0.1 -- and the leading 0 says it is
still beta. Chrome requires at least two dot-separated numbers here and
the tooling elsewhere assumes three, so the manifest carries the padded
form 0.1.0: same version, trailing zero added. Bump the SECOND digit for
each iteration (0.2 -> 0.2.0, 0.3 -> 0.3.0). The major digit goes to 1
only when Peter says the beta is over.
Three places to change, and nowhere else: this field, VERSION in
host/websdrsync_host.py, and the zip file name. The top bar reads the
version from this manifest at load and drops the trailing .0.
ADDING A RECEIVER
1. add its origin to host_permissions and to content_scripts[0].matches below
2. add it to the SDRS array at the top of console.js, with coverage in kHz
3. reload the extension on chrome://extensions
PORTS ARE NOT PART OF A MATCH PATTERN. Chrome match patterns cannot contain a
port and match every port on the host, so one entry per HOST covers all of a
site's receivers -- sdr.websdrmaasbree.nl:8901 (low) and :8902 (high) are both
covered by the single sdr.websdrmaasbree.nl entry. The port still has to be
right in the SDRS url in console.js, which is where it actually connects.
bridge.js only answers messages from this extension's own console page, so it
does nothing at all on a receiver you open normally.
